title: Prompt Tiles sandbox — personal PRD sketch
content:
Quick brain dump / rough PRD for an experiment: 'Prompt Tiles' — tiny reusable prompt snippets (visual tiles) that users can assemble, preview, and measure cost/latency impact before sending to the model.

Context / motivation:
- Our customers constantly rebuild prompt scaffolding across flows. Reuse is low and teams over-index on large monolithic prompts.
- Developer DX / Product UX asks: quicker authoring, safer reuse, and explicit unit economics (token/cost/latency) at composition time.
- Related threads: #prompt-savings (Slack), DX-927 (jira) for prompt-lib requirements.

High-level idea:
- A lightweight UI + backend model abstraction where a user creates "tiles" (snippets) with metadata and constraints. Tiles can be dragged into a composition canvas to form a prompt pipeline.
- Each tile stores: title, language, role (system / assistant / user), parametrized fields, estimated token delta (preview), cost multiplier, optional eval tests.
- Canvas provides: inline token count, cost estimate (per-run, 95p latency), per-tile explainability (why this tile matters), rollbacks to previous versions.

Primary goals:
- Reduce duplication by enabling snippet reuse across flows and teams.
- Surface cost/latency tradeoffs at authoring time so product engineers can make informed choices.
- Provide basic safety checks (blacklisted phrases, redaction hints) before composition is deployed.

User stories (rough):
- As a product engineer, I want to save a common instruction as a tile so I can reuse it in multiple assistant flows.
- As a PM, I want to preview token and cost impact of adding a tile so I can evaluate tradeoffs quickly.
- As an SRE/customer-reliability engineer, I want to pin a tile to a quantized model variant so the behavior is stable across deploys.
- As an evaluator, I want to attach a small unit test to a tile (input -> expected output properties) so regressions can be detected when tile or model changes.

Low-fidelity flow:
1) Create tile: new tile modal -> title, role, body (text), params (template vars), tags, safety checks.
2) Save tile -> stored in user/org library with versioning.
3) Compose canvas: drag N tiles -> order matters; show concatenated preview with token breakdown by tile.
4) Preview: emulate a single run with sample inputs; show: token count, estimated cost (hosted pricing), latency estimate (95p) based on model profile.
5) Save composition as a preset route/flow; optionally export to YAML that routing/runtime can consume (for dedicated/private).

Acceptance criteria (first iteration):
- [ ] Basic tile CRUD in UI + persist to backend (owner-scoped).
- [ ] Canvas composition shows token counts per tile and total.
- [ ] Cost estimate shows per-run cost (USD) and a simple latency bracket (fast/medium/slow) using model profiles.
- [ ] Tile versioning with ability to revert to last v1/v2.
- [ ] Simple unit test attach: user can store 1 example input and 1 assertion (contains / regex / JSON path existence).

Data model sketch (for API / runtime integration) — keep simple for now:
- Tile: id, name, owner_org, role, body_template, params[], safety_flags[], version, created_at, last_modified, tags[]
- Composition: id, owner_org, ordered_tile_ids[], name, preview_sample_input, last_test_result

Edge cases / open questions:
- How to handle context sizing? If composition > model max tokens, show warning and suggest compaction (compress tile or switch model).
- Do we allow dynamic branching tiles (if/else logic) or keep strictly linear for v1? Prefer linear first.
- Ownership + sharing: private by default; org-shared library and team-scoped libraries? Need policy design.
- Security: tiles may accidentally contain secrets (dev environment). Add scanning and "mark as sensitive" flag.

Metrics to watch (MVP):
- # of tiles created / org per month (adoption)
- % of compositions that re-use at least 1 tile (reuse rate)
- Average token reduction (if we add compaction recommendations)
- Time-to-author (median time from new composition start to save)
- Regression rate from attached unit tests (how many tests fail after model/ tile updates)

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: users treat tiles as immutable contracts and expect runtime stability. Mitigation: explicit pinning + a "breaking change" audit log and rollout strategy.
- Risk: UX complexity (too many knobs). Mitigation: defaults + progressive disclosure: simple mode = name/body; advanced = params/variants.
- Risk: inaccurate cost estimates. Mitigation: show ranges and link to realtime billing metrics in Console.

Implementation notes / iteration plan:
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): internal prototype — React canvas with drag/drop, local storage of tiles, tokenization via existing token-count lib. No backend persistence.
- Phase 1 (4–6 weeks): backend tile service (CRUD), org library, basic cost model integration (hosted model profiles), attach 1 example test. Integrate with Console to show usage metrics.
- Phase 2 (quarter 2): shareable libraries, collaborator permissions, composition export -> routing config for Dedicated/Private, evaluation harness for tile tests.

Possible quick wins to demo to partners:
- Demo 1: Create 3 tiles (system preface, instruction snip, user template) and show cost delta when swapping system preface with a heavier paraphrase.
- Demo 2: Attach a small unit test to a tile and run it across 3 model versions to show regression detection.

Open TODOs (action items):
- Talk to Solutions Eng to validate sharing & permission needs (assign to Kai).
- Slack poll: would customers want org-only library or public template marketplace? (post in #product-feedback).
- Spike: measure accuracy of our latency estimates vs real previously-recorded 95p numbers (ask SRE for sample traces).

Notes / tangential ideas:
- Could tie a "cost budget" to a composition and run linting that suggests cheaper equivalents (eg shorter synonyms, compressive prompts).
- Consider a CLI export to include tiles in IaC for Private deployments (tile YAML -> included in infra).
- Think about tile semantics for multimodal prompts (image + text tiles) — out of scope for v1.

References / links:
- Jira: DX-927 (prompt-reuse patterns), PROD-4821 (costing-model improvements)
- Confluence: Prompt Reusability Notes (linked above)

Rough mockups sketched in my notebook — will take a screenshot and add here next pass.

Notes to self: keep scope small. MVP needs to feel useful for a single engineer creating 2–3 flows, not enterprise catalog plumbing.
